newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary decides to sell off shipping firm MAHART.
newsitem.headline: Hungary decides to sell off shipping firm MAHART.

text.p: The Hungarian government has decided to sell large minority stakes in the national shipping company MAHART Rt and its subsidiaries, a government spokesman told a news conference following Thursday's cabinet meeting.
Kiss Elemer said that in the first phase of the privatisation, stakes in MAHART's subsidiaries would be sold.
The units are MAHART PassNave Kft, MAHART Seatrade Kft and MAHART Balatoni Hajozasi Rt, which respectively deal with shipping on rivers, on the sea and on Lake Balaton.
In Seatrade and PassNave a 49 percent stake will be offered, while 70 percent of Balatoni's shares will be sold.
These stakes include the sale to the employees of nine percent in Seatrade and PassNave and four percent in Balatoni.
The state will retain 50 percent plus one vote in MAHART Rt, which coordinates Hungarian shipping and ship maintenance.
Following the subsidiaries' sell-off, a 46 percent stake will be offered to investors, while the remaining four percent will be sold to employees, Kiss said.
The government said in a statement that privatisation should assure capital injections for the shipping companies to finance necessary developments.
The timing and the conditions of the sales will be worked out by the state privatisation agency APV.
